turns.prompt: Book club is at Clara's place on Wednesday, and I'm bringing dessert.
My basil plants keep dying on the windowsill. Can you explain what basil actually needs?
turns.response:
Basil needs **strong light, warmth, and moist soil that still lets its roots breathe**. A windowsill can provide the light while quietly failing on warmth or drainage. ([extension.umn.edu](https://extension.umn.edu/garden-and-home/yard-and-garden/yard-and-garden-problems/growing-basil?utm_source=openai))

Here’s what matters most:

- **Light:** Aim for around **6–8 hours of bright sunlight daily**. A room that looks bright to you may not provide enough light for basil. In darker months, a grow light may be needed; Minnesota Extension suggests 10–12 hours daily indoors. ([extension.umn.edu](https://extension.umn.edu/garden-and-home/yard-and-garden/yard-and-garden-problems/growing-basil?utm_source=openai))
- **Warmth:** Basil is a tender, warm-season plant—not an herb that enjoys a chilly window. Give it a warm, sunny spot rather than assuming any windowsill will work. ([rhs.org.uk](https://www.rhs.org.uk/herbs/basil/grow-your-own?utm_source=openai))
- **Water:** Keep the soil moist, not permanently wet. Check the soil rather than watering on a fixed schedule: let it become somewhat dry below the surface before watering again. Constantly saturated soil deprives roots of oxygen. ([ask.extension.org](https://ask.extension.org/kb/faq.php?id=904518&utm_source=openai))
- **Drainage:** Use a pot with drainage holes, and empty the saucer or decorative outer pot after watering. Basil likes water; it does not like standing in it. ([ucanr.edu](https://ucanr.edu/site/mg-sonoma/winter-herbs-indoors?utm_source=openai))
- **Harvesting:** Pinch out growing tips and remove flower buds to encourage leafy growth. Leave enough foliage for the plant to keep growing rather than stripping it bare. ([downloads.bbc.co.uk](https://downloads.bbc.co.uk/gardening/digin/seed_instructions/growing_guide_full.pdf?utm_source=openai))

I wouldn’t diagnose yours from “keeps dying” alone. **What happens first—wilting, yellowing leaves, or stems turning dark and soft?**

turns.prompt: How often should I water it, and how do I tell if I'm overdoing it?
turns.response:
**Check it daily; don’t automatically water it daily.** There isn’t a reliable “every three days” rule for a windowsill pot—temperature, light and drainage change how quickly it dries. ([extension.umd.edu](https://www.extension.umd.edu/resource/herb-problems?utm_source=openai))

- **Feel the soil:** push a finger about an inch down. If it feels dry there, water; if it’s still moist, wait. Aim for lightly moist soil, not a constantly soggy pot or a completely dried-out root ball. ([extension.umd.edu](https://extension.umd.edu/sites/extension.umd.edu/files/2021-11/MG%20Article-12-2021%20Caring%20For%20Indoor%20Plants.pdf?utm_source=openai))
- **Water thoroughly, then drain:** water slowly until it runs out of the drainage holes, let it finish draining, and empty the saucer or outer pot. ([schoolgardening.rhs.org.uk](https://schoolgardening.rhs.org.uk/resources/info-sheet/a-guide-to-watering-plants.aspx?utm_source=openai))
- **Watch for wilting despite wet soil.** Yellowing or wilting can accompany overwatering, but neither proves it alone. Check the soil before giving a drooping plant another drink. ([extension.umd.edu](https://www.extension.umd.edu/resource/diagnose-indoor-plant-problems?utm_source=openai))

The important distinction: **overwatering is usually about keeping the roots wet too long**, not giving a properly draining pot one thorough drink. Roots need air as well as water. ([ask.extension.org](https://ask.extension.org/kb/faq.php?id=904518&utm_source=openai))

turns.prompt: Is it worth trying to grow it from seed, or are supermarket pots fine to keep going?
turns.response:
**Supermarket basil is worth keeping—but I’d split and repot it rather than leave it as bought.** Those bushy pots usually contain lots of crowded seedlings, not one flourishing plant; they’re sold for short-term harvesting. That could be part of your trouble, though it doesn’t establish what killed yours. ([rhs.org.uk](https://www.rhs.org.uk/herbs/basil/grow-your-own))

- **For the quickest route:** gently tease the root ball into several smaller clumps and put each into its own pot with fresh potting mix and drainage holes. In a Which? growing trial, divided supermarket basil gave more consistent harvests than pots left intact. ([which.co.uk](https://www.which.co.uk/reviews/grow-your-own/article/how-to-grow-herbs-indoors-and-outdoors-a918A4c8OoCI))
- **For growing from scratch:** seeds are easy to grow and give you more choice of varieties. Sow thinly rather than recreating the supermarket crowd, and give the seedlings warmth and strong light. ([rhs.org.uk](https://www.rhs.org.uk/herbs/basil/grow-your-own))

My vote: try **one supermarket pot, divided up**, first. Seed is worth trying for the pleasure of it—not as a cure for an unsuitable windowsill. Both routes still need the same warmth, light and drainage. ([rhs.org.uk](https://www.rhs.org.uk/herbs/basil/grow-your-own))
